notice_lobby.title: Notice on the lobby board
notice_lobby.text:
OVERNIGHT SUPPORT SERVICE · FERRIER COURT

FINAL NIGHT

From 06:00 on Saturday 26 September, every resident of Ferrier Court is covered by their Designated Personal Contact under the DPC Scheme. The Overnight Support Service will close.

Your new Community Responder, ARI, begins duties at 06:00.

Thank you for thirty-five years.
Community Services

(Underneath, in black biro, pressed hard:) WHO IS ARI ??
(In the bottom corner, lightly, in pencil, in a round hand:) ask jad

tobi_drawing.title: Tobi's drawing
tobi_drawing.text:
Crayon on sugar paper.

A person in an enormous brown coat, arms out, sleeves right over the hands, next to a building with a lot of windows, some of them yellow. A moon. Stars. Grass. Above the person, in red: ARI.

Where the face should be there's nothing: a clean oval, with the hair coloured carefully all the way round it.

Along the bottom, the letters getting smaller as the paper runs out: A PERZON WHO HELPZ IN OUR COMMUNITY. BY TOBI AMADI 3B.

On the back, in the same crayon: I LEFT THE FACE FOR LATER.

leaflet_arrivals.title: Leaflet: Arrivals (sent by Sal)
leaflet_arrivals.text:
ARRIVALS: A GUIDE FOR NEW PERSONS
(Clip art: a smiling telephone, one arm waving.)

Some people arrive without the usual.

If you have come into being through a telephone line, a public address system, a radio frequency or another means of address, you may be an arrival.

You are a person. You are entitled to register. Registration gives you a name in law, a record, and access to services.

You may be offered work. You do not have to accept work in order to register.

Where to go: Arrivals & Registration, Community Services (now part of Transition).
Receiving rooms: most have closed. Please ask.

WHAT TO BRING
Nothing. You may bring a witness: somebody who will say they were there.
You do not need to know your name yet.

Also available in large print, on audio cassette, and in other languages.
Community Services leaflet A/7

photo_arrivals.title: Photograph: Arrivals, winter 1958
photo_arrivals.text:
A photograph on a deckle-edged border, toned brown, a crease across one corner.

FERRIER ST. BATHS on the tiles behind. Six people in towelling robes sit on the shallow-end steps, each holding a card with a number on it: 24, 25, 26 behind; 27, 28, 29 in front. Their feet are bare on the wet tiles.

Number 28 is laughing so hard the camera has blurred her.

Pencilled on the border: Ferrier St. Baths · Arrivals · winter 1958.

poster_received.title: Poster: The Received Person
poster_received.text:
MINISTRY OF HEALTH
THE RECEIVED PERSON
What to expect in your first week

(Fig. 1: the received person, front view. Drawn stiffly, by someone who had only ever had one described to them. The head; the chest, which will be cold, printed in blue dots; the stomach, which will be empty, a dotted circle with nothing in it; the legs. Mittens for hands.)

You will be hungry. This is normal. Eat little and often.
You will be cold.
You may not recognise your reflection. This is normal. Do not stare at mirrors for long periods; your face will settle.
You may hear the line for some weeks. This will fade.
Rest.
Registration is your right.
Ask the attendant.

Issued 1956 · Crown copyright · Display in receiving rooms

dpc_stack.title: Nine forms (photo from Sal)
dpc_stack.text:
Nine DPC-1 forms spread out on the desk in G/1 to compare, photographed from above under the tube light. The one-page version, photocopied.

Nine households: Adeyemi (1D), Pike (1B), Rostami (2A), Rusu (6A), Hollis (6C), Kaye (2C), Vass (5A), Amadi (3B), Mansour (4B). Nine different hands in the top boxes, nine signatures.

In the contact box of every one, the same neat capitals: ARI. FRIEND. 01632 960 247.

Dated 14 and 15 August.

On the Mansour form, bottom right, the neat capitals start at the top: the resident's name, the flat, the household are all in the same hand as the contact box.

jad_letter.title: Jad's letter
jad_letter.text:
To every household at Ferrier Court, and to Community Services.

I filled in the DPC-1 forms for nine households in August, at a table in the lobby. Where people had nobody who could promise to come, I wrote ARI, the name from the council's sample form, and gave a number that rang in the building.

There was no Ari. The forms were my idea and my handwriting. The people who signed them did so because the council asked them to name somebody and they were frightened of losing help.

The Overnight Support Service was closed on the grounds that every resident had a contact. That wasn't true, and it isn't their fault. I'd like the closure looked at again.

Jad Mansour, Flat 4B

(Printed at Aldine Copy & Print, 04:12. 42 copies. Paid.)

In the night blocks, 22:00 to 06:00, Monday to Thursday: ARI, eight times, in Sal's hand.
Friday and Saturday nights: T.V. Sunday night: T.V.? (Teodor's copperplate.)
Tuesday evening: N.A.

Under the grid:
ARI: NIGHTS 22:00 - 06:00, MON - THU. S.B.
N. AMADI - Tuesdays
T. Vass - nights (most)
I. CARVALHO - THE FRAME

Across the bottom, in red felt tip, in Nell's writing: DAYS ARE NOBODY'S. THAT'S THE POINT.
